payload.fact: SaaS-OMS proven pattern - THREE INDEPENDENT ORDER STATUS AXES (ADR-06): payment_status (unpaid/partially_paid/paid/refunded), fulfilment_status (new/allocated/picked/packed/shipped/delivered), exception_status (none/on_hold/cancelled/returned). Each enum owns allowedNext(); a cross-axis OrderStateMachine owns rules no single enum can know. Solves COD packed-but-unpaid and shipped-then-refunded without hybrid states. Status columns excluded from fillable; only the state machine writes them via forceFill inside DB::transaction

payload.fact: SaaS-OMS proven tenancy pattern: single DB, row-scoped, NO package. BelongsToTenant auto-stamps on create, refuses cross-tenant creates, makes tenant_id immutable. Single greppable escape hatch Model::acrossTenants(). NO Gate::before super-admin bypass. Editing commission_ranks.rate or commission_settings.rate retroactively changes what a re-run of a CLOSED period produces. payload.fact: COMMISSION ANTI-PATTERN: commission calculated INLINE inside a payment-gateway callback (AgentStockit PaymentController:36, SAAS-Agent PaymentController:208) with NO unique index and NO idempotency check. Gateways retry callbacks, so this creates duplicate money. AgentStockit PayoutService::createBatch() also sweeps approved commissions into payout_items but never flips them to paid - running it twice pays the same commission twice. Fix: queued job keyed on order + DB unique index on (order_id,user_id,type,level)

Money rows must never vanish. Fix: reversed state + contra entry referencing the original, event-driven on order cancel/return/refund

payload.chosen: attributions + attribution_touches tables, polymorphic over Lead/Customer/Order. Every touch recorded. Commission credit goes to the FIRST touch (the marketer who originally generated the lead). Attribution resolved from the lead trail then FROZEN onto the order at creation

payload.title: Commission pays a percentage of FULL gross margin (sales - cost - shipping - fees - ad spend)
payload.chosen: Default commission plan strategy is PercentageOfMargin where margin = sales minus product cost minus shipping/postage minus payment fees minus allocated ad spend. Commission accrues PROVISIONALLY on estimates and is RESTATED at period close against reconciled actuals, with the restatement emitted as an audited adjustment entry, never a silent re-run

payload.title: Commission rules immutable and effective-dated; every commission stamps its rule version and basis
payload.chosen: commission_rules + commission_rule_versions with valid_from/valid_to, immutable after creation. Every commission row persists rule_version_id, basis_amount, rate_type, rate_applied and calc_inputs jsonb, plus a commission_sources join to every contributing order line. Calculation runs in a queued job keyed on the order behind a DB unique index. Reversal is a contra entry, never a delete. Payout posts to Finance in the same transaction

payload.fact: REPRODUCED 2026-08-15 in Brand New ERP P0: Pest's expect($x)->not->toContain('a', 'my failure message') PASSES UNCONDITIONALLY because the second argument is parsed as another EXPECTED VALUE, not a message. A company_id mass-assignment guard written this way sat green while the violation was present. Only a deliberately planted violation exposed it. Fix: expect(in_array($needle, $haystack, true))->toBeFalse('message'). General rule: toContain/toContainEqual take variadic expected values - never pass a message to them. Every negated guard assertion must be proven by mutation before it is trusted

payload.fact: SELF-INFLICTED 2026-08-15 Brand New ERP P0: a line-based Python comment-stripper silently corrupted 12 PHP files. Cause: a single-line docblock '/** @return array */' matched the block-OPEN branch, set drop_block=True and continued WITHOUT testing the same line for the closing '*/', so every following code line was swallowed until the next '*/'. Files were left syntactically invalid; the failure surfaced only as a confusing Pest DatasetMissing error, not as a parse error at the edit site. RULE: any script that rewrites source must run a syntax check (php -l / node --check / python -m py_compile) over EVERY touched file in the same step, and must handle open-and-close-on-one-line before the open-only branch. This is the same class as the PowerShell BOM anti-pattern - a mechanical rewrite that reports success while producing unparseable files

payload.fact: LARAVEL 11/12 TRAP found 2026-08-15: $middleware->priority([...]) in bootstrap/app.php REPLACES the entire framework default priority list, it does not merge. Passing two classes left a 2-entry list with Authenticate absent, so a route middleware hoisted to position 0 ran BEFORE authentication and its abort(401) pre-empted the guest redirect. Symptom was a guest getting 401 instead of a redirect to /login, which reads like an auth-config problem, not a priority problem. Correct API: prependToPriorityList($before, $insert) / appendToPriorityList($after, $insert), which preserve the 13 defaults. Also note Illuminate\\Auth\\Middleware\\Authenticate is NOT in the default priority list, so it must be inserted explicitly if ordering against it matters. Guard with a test asserting index(Authenticate) < index(YourMiddleware) < index(SubstituteBindings)
payload.source: Reproduced and fixed in Brand New ERP P1; verified priority list went from 2 entries to 13 with correct ordering

payload.fact: PROCESS RULE reinforced 2026-08-15: a scripted string replace that does not ASSERT it matched is a silent no-op. Twice in this project a python replace ran, printed a success message, and changed nothing because a formatter (Pint) had already rewritten the anchor text - once leaving a broken middleware priority in place while I believed it fixed. Rule: every scripted edit asserts count==1 before writing, or uses an edit tool that errors on no-match. A rewrite that cannot fail is a rewrite that cannot be trusted

payload.fact: ELOQUENT TRAP found 2026-08-15: a database column DEFAULT does not populate an in-memory model. Customer::create(['code'=>..,'name'=>..]) left $customer->currency NULL even though the column defaults to 'MYR', because the default is applied by Postgres on INSERT and never read back unless the model is refreshed. A price resolver then received null where a currency string was required and threw a TypeError. FIX: mirror every meaningful DB default in the model's protected $attributes array so the in-memory object and the persisted row agree before any refresh

payload.fact: P3 ORDER DESIGN (Brand New ERP): three independent status axes ported from SaaS-OMS ADR-06 and extended. payment_status unpaid/partially_paid/paid/refunded; fulfilment_status draft/pending/approved/allocated/picked/packed/shipped/delivered/completed; exception_status none/on_hold/cancelled/returned. Each enum owns allowedNext(); OrderStateMachine owns the cross-axis rules. FIXED the known OMS defect P1-25: the machine refuses PaymentStatus::Paid while paid_amount < total, so status can never contradict the money. Status columns and money totals are both excluded from Order fillable; the state machine is the sole status writer and OrderService the sole money writer, both enforced by architecture tests proven with planted violations

payload.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - reasonAgainst() returning a human sentence instead of a boolean. OrderStateMachine::reasonAgainst(Order, BackedEnum): ?string returns null when legal and a merchant-readable sentence when not, e.g. 'This order has already shipped. Record a return instead of cancelling it.' canTransition() is then just reasonAgainst() === null, and availableTransitions() filters on it, so the UI, the API error and the guard all share one source of truth. The same idiom drives OrderMutabilityPolicy::reasonLocked() and is the intended shape for the commission engine's explanation in P6
payload.source: Ported from SaaS-OMS and implemented in Brand New ERP P3

payload.fact: LARAVEL 11/12 TRAP found 2026-08-15: framework AUTO-DISCOVERS listeners in app/Listeners (any class with a handle() method type-hinting an event). Adding an explicit Event::listen for the same event/listener pair registers it TWICE, so every side effect runs twice. In Brand New ERP P4 this silently reserved stock twice per order line - a duplicate-inventory bug that looked like a reservation logic error, not a wiring error. Fix: rely on auto-discovery OR disable it, never both. GUARD: assert Event::getListeners(YourEvent::class) has exactly the expected count; the guard was proven by planting the duplicate registration and confirming both the guard and the behavioural test fail
payload.source: Reproduced in Brand New ERP P4: 2 reservations for 1 order line; fixed and guarded

payload.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - reservation-based inventory with a provable invariant. stock.on_hand is signed (a real warehouse goes negative after a miscount; refusing to represent it turns a counting error into a 500). available = on_hand - reserved is DERIVED, never stored. Reserving changes only reserved; only commit changes on_hand and writes an append-only movement. Every on_hand change writes a movement carrying quantity_delta and a denormalised balance_after, so SUM(quantity_delta) == on_hand is a testable invariant per stock line. All mutations take a blocking SELECT FOR UPDATE on the stock row (not SKIP LOCKED - last-unit scarcity is queue-and-wait), and commit/release take their own lock so a reservation cannot be discharged twice
payload.source: Implemented in Brand New ERP P4; oversell reproduces on 3 of 3 runs when the lock is removed
